title: The Rise

segments.text: It all started with a botanist. In 1593, Carolus Clusius planted his tulips in the new botanical garden of Leiden.
Rare flowers, unpredictable colours, and by 1634, speculators had entered the market.
Contracts changed hands in taverns, sometimes five times, for bulbs still in the ground.
In 1841, Charles Mackay wrote that everyone joined in, down to chimney-sweeps and old clothes-women.
At the peak, a single bulb could cost more than ten times what a skilled craftsman earned in a year.
Everyone, it seemed, was about to get rich.

summary_for_next: From Clusius's Leiden garden (1593) to speculators (1634) and tavern contracts that changed hands five times; Mackay later claimed everyone traded.
